history.period: Ancient; date of construction not documented
history.summary: Sitamani is an ancient heritage and pilgrimage site in Korba city, near the railway station, centred on three caves formed by cutting into the rocks at the side of a trench. One cave enshrines ancient idols of Ram, Sita and Lakshman; local belief holds that Rama passed through this area during his vanvas (exile), and footprints found at the site are believed to be Sita's — hence the name Sitamani. Near the caves is an ancient stone inscription mentioning 'Vedputra Shrivardhan, resident of Ashtadwar'. A large Ram Sita temple stands beside the caves (sources disagree on whether it is to the right or the left — verify), along with several smaller shrines holding ancient idols of gods and goddesses. Coordinates are a locality-level estimate for Sitamani near Korba railway station and are APPROXIMATE (unverified against a map pin).

name: Sitamani Temples and Caves
town_description: Korba is a major industrial city in Chhattisgarh, often called the power capital of the state, with large coal mines and thermal power plants (including NTPC and BALCO) around it. It lies on the banks of the Hasdeo river, which also shapes its religious geography, with riverbank shrines such as Sarvamangala and the Kanki temple nearby. The city is well connected by rail and road; the nearest airport is Swami Vivekananda Airport in Raipur. Sitamani is a locality within Korba city, close to the railway station.
